topic.title: Sizing Thermal Solution for PL2 – Recommendations

ul.li: The heat pipe should cover all the cores to maximize turbo durations and ensure every core is cooled during single core workloads.

To select the heat pipe for your design, thermal modeling can help to determine how much heat is going into the heat pipe, as it is <100% of the PL2. Use this power to select a heat pipe that can handle it, without drying out.
Qmax should include proper de-rating for final heat pipe geometry including factors such as bends, length and thickness, according to the heat pipe manufacturer's spec sheet.
Intel recommends testing your heat pipe to assure no dry-out occurs, specially if you decide to operate a heat pipe above it's Qmax for the short duration of PL2 events.
Using 2 heat pipes, 3 heat pipes or vapor chambers for high PL2s is recommended to avoid heat pipe dry-out.
The fan RPM during the PL2 event may not affect transient thermal performance for the first 5 to 10 seconds.
Reducing rest of system power will enable lower starting temperatures and could lead to longer turbo durations.
TIM performance optimization has a significant impact on transient performance. Refer to section and for more details.
Cold plate thickness has significant impact on transient thermal performance. Refer to section and for details.
Thicker heat pipes increase maximum heat carrying capacity of heat pipes (Qmax).
Thermal engineer can choose to trade-off cold plate thickness for heat pipe z-height.
Cold plate width ( and heat exchanger thermal mass also has relatively minor effects on transient thermals.
